title: Injectivity of the quadruple encoding
statement: For bit strings $\alpha,x,\beta,y$ and natural numbers $n,t,m,s$, if $\langle\alpha,\langle x,\langle 1^n,1^t\rangle\rangle\rangle=\langle\beta,\langle y,\langle 1^m,1^s\rangle\rangle\rangle$, then $\alpha=\beta$, $x=y$, $n=m$, and $t=s$.
hypotheses_covered: The two nested encodings are equal
replaced: For bit strings $\alpha, x, \beta, y$ and $n, t, m, s \in \mathbb{N}$, if $\langle\alpha,\langle x,\langle 1^n,1^t\rangle\rangle\rangle = \langle\beta,\langle y,\langle 1^m,1^s\rangle\rangle\rangle$, where $\langle a,b\rangle$ is the self-delimiting pair encoding and $1^k$ the word of $k$ ones, then $\alpha = \beta$, $x = y$, $n = m$ and $t = s$.
